title: Two Ways to Fail
description: The same bad timezone name is rejected two different ways depending on which endpoint you ask — one loudly, one quietly. A dispatcher relying on the async job endpoint to behave like the synchronous one is in for a surprise.
successCondition: Send the same invalid IANA timeZone (e.g. "Mars/Olympus_Mons") to both endpoints with an otherwise-identical query: GET /api/reporting/summary returns a 500 with error.code "INTERNAL_ERROR" (the Intl failure is uncaught at that layer), while POST /api/reporting/jobs instead returns 202 and the job is accepted — polling GET /api/reporting/jobs/:id afterward shows status transition to "failed" with a non-null failureReason, never "ready". Document that the two endpoints do not fail the same way for identical bad input.
hints: The async path wraps report generation in a try/catch that writes status "failed" (see apps/api/src/modules/reporting/service.ts) — the sync /summary path has no equivalent guard.
Give the background job a moment to run before polling GET /jobs/:id — it starts as "pending" and only flips to "failed" once the queued work actually executes.
